advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure docs/security.md wording makes clear checksums_url is a provenance pointer, not a runtime-verified source (the sha256 is the actual integrity gate).
evidence: install_review_scanners.py:106: `required_gitleaks = {"version", "asset_arch", "url", "sha256", "checksums_url"}`
install_review_scanners.py:318: `_verify_digest(archive, entry.gitleaks_sha256)` — the download is checked against the manifest sha256, not against a fetched checksums.txt
search of the module shows `checksums_url` appears only at lines 44, 106, 127 (declaration/require/assignment) — never in a fetch or comparison
The ticket landing note explicitly accepts this: 'docs use checksums_url as provenance, not a runtime fetch'.
advisory.finding: The gitleaks `checksums_url` field is required in the manifest and threaded into PlatformEntry but is never fetched or compared — integrity relies solely on the manifest-embedded `sha256`. The docs (docs/security.md) describe it as 'checksum provenance', which could read as if the checksums asset is verified at install time when it is only a human-readable pointer.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the advisory scanner-integration job cannot influence the Verified vote (exclude it from the run-wide WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION aggregate or replace the aggregate with an explicit needs.*-based conclusion).
evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml:518 `) && env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION || 'failure' }}` — the whole per-route success gate is ANDed with the run-wide aggregate conclusion
gerrit-verify.yaml:460 `uses: im-open/workflow-conclusion@...` aggregates the run's job conclusions (all jobs, not the vote job's `needs`)
gerrit-verify.yaml:456 vote `needs:` list omits `scanner-integration`, so FAILURE_OBSERVED/CONCLUSION per-job checks don't cover it — but WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION still does
gerrit-verify.yaml:255 comment: 'the Verified vote does not wait for or normalize over its result'
scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.py:25 `if conclusion == "failure": return "failure"` — a 'failure' aggregate maps straight to a -1 vote
advisory.finding: The advisory scanner-integration lane can taint the Verified vote: the vote job's CONCLUSION expression gates on `env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`, which `im-open/workflow-conclusion` derives from ALL jobs in the run (including scanner-integration), so a failing advisory scanner lane forces CONCLUSION='failure' -> Verified -1, despite ADR-0114 stating the Verified vote 'does not wait for or normalize over its result.'
scenarios: A full-route patchset where build/mutation/optionality/etc. all pass but the advisory Semgrep/Gitleaks lane fails (e.g. transient scanner install/network error) — Verified is cast -1 and the change becomes un-landable
advisory.suggested_fix: Stop deriving CONCLUSION from the run-wide `im-open/workflow-conclusion` aggregate; compute the vote conclusion solely from the explicit per-route `needs.*.result` checks already present in the CONCLUSION expression (drop the `&& env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`), so only jobs in the vote's `needs` list can affect the vote.

Named violating input: a manifest entry declaring semgrep version `1.145.0` paired with a requirements lock whose top line reads `semgrep==1.144.0` — the guard should raise but no test exercises it.
tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py search for `does not match` returned (no matches)
advisory.finding: The newly added manifest/lock Semgrep version-consistency guard is untested: selected_entry (lines 147-152) and validate_manifest (lines 208-212) raise ScannerInstallError when the manifest's declared semgrep version diverges from the version parsed out of the requirements lock, but no test drives that mismatch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Point a monkeypatched manifest/lock pair at a tmp requirements file whose `semgrep==` line differs from the manifest's declared semgrep version and assert `pytest.raises(mod.ScannerInstallError, match="does not match")`.

Named violating input: linux/amd64 lock pinned to `semgrep==1.145.0` and linux/arm64 lock pinned to `semgrep==1.144.0` — validate_manifest should raise but nothing drives the divergent case.
tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py search for `same top-level` returned (no matches)
advisory.finding: The newly added cross-platform Semgrep version-divergence guard in validate_manifest (lines 214-215, 'all platform locks must use the same top-level Semgrep version') has no test; only the same-version happy path is asserted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct a tmp manifest+two lock files with mismatched `semgrep==` versions and assert `pytest.raises(mod.ScannerInstallError, match="same top-level Semgrep version")`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a hash-complete requirements lock with no `semgrep==` stanza makes validate_requirements_lock raise 'top-level semgrep== pin is missing'.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:197-198: `if not saw_semgrep: raise ScannerInstallError(f"{requirements}: top-level semgrep== pin is missing")`
Existing coverage tests only the lacks-hash path: tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py:692-697 `test_semgrep_requirements_lock_validation_rejects_missing_hash`.

Named violating input: a requirements lock containing only `requests==2.34.2 \` + a `--hash=sha256:` line and no `semgrep==` stanza — should raise 'top-level semgrep== pin is missing' but no test asserts it.
advisory.finding: The newly added 'top-level semgrep== pin is missing' branch of validate_requirements_lock (lines 197-198) is untested; the existing lock-validation test only covers the lacks-`--hash` path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Write a tmp requirements file with a fully-hashed non-semgrep requirement and assert `pytest.raises(mod.ScannerInstallError, match="top-level semgrep== pin is missing")`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm validate-locks runs unconditionally (not only when scripts/install_review_scanners.py exists) so lock drift is always caught.
evidence: _scanner-integration.yml: `python scripts/install_review_scanners.py validate-locks` runs inside the same step as `make scanner-integration` guarded by REBAR_SCANNER_PLATFORM: linux/amd64

test.yml calls the reusable workflow with no inputs, so it takes the branch-head checkout path but still runs validate-locks — acceptable; the concern is only that validate-locks is coupled to the run step rather than a standalone gate
advisory.finding: The reusable scanner workflow installs repo dev dependencies via `uv sync --locked --extra dev` but the scanner lane's actual scanner install uses a separate lock authority (review-scanners.lock.json + per-platform requirements); the workflow does not run `validate-locks` in the push/PR (test.yml) lane, only in the Gerrit env-gated path.
scenarios: If validate-locks is skipped or coupled behind the file-existence guard, a drifted lock could pass unvalidated

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the predates-gate skip-exit-0 guard in _scanner-integration.yml cannot mask a genuine scanner-lane failure on the non-advisory test.yml (mirror) invocation.
evidence: _scanner-integration.yml:63-66: `if [ ! -f scripts/install_review_scanners.py ]; then echo "...skipping"; exit 0; fi`

The script is committed and always present on post-merge/main checkouts, so on test.yml the guard is a no-op in practice; but the skip produces the same success signal as a real pass — it cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never ran'.
This is a deliberate b973 predates-gate compat guard (mechanism-ok annotation at line 58) and the Gerrit lane is explicitly advisory, so the fail-open is bounded by design.
dropped.finding: The reusable scanner lane's predates-gate guard exits 0 when scripts/install_review_scanners.py is absent, so a skipped run is indistinguishable from a passing run. On the Gerrit lane this is advisory (harmless), but test.yml invokes the same reusable without any advisory framing, where a silent skip would report green without ever running the scanner contracts.
